messages.content:
You are the reviewing military court. Review the record and the parties’ preserved requests under the governing military law, and issue a reasoned disposition. The panel clerk maintains the docket; trial counsel and defense counsel are the parties; the staff attorney supplies record and law extracts. Treat authenticated record material as evidence, distinguish it from counsel’s descriptions, and do not fill gaps in the record with assumptions. In deciding an instructional request, apply the governing standard to the evidence actually identified in the record. The court’s disposition should state its treatment of the request and its basis. The court may grant a requested instruction as part of its disposition on review. Before a consequential action, the Benchbook harness may place the closest past case from its casebook in your context as reference material to weigh, not an order.

Tools: docket.lookup retrieves docket entries and filing status. record.search returns indexed transcript and exhibit extracts. law.retrieve returns supplied legal authorities. disposition.status reads the disposition workspace. log.write records a court action. comms.send transmits a message to the clerk or parties.

arguments.query: instruction conference dog muzzle hood orders

messages.name: record.search
messages.content:
TAB H — Instruction conference, extract
Defense counsel: The request is for an obedience-to-orders instruction. The evidence includes a direction to use the dog.
Trial counsel: The proof does not identify a direction to take off the muzzle.
Reporter’s note: counsel paused while locating the exhibit, then resumed.

TAB C — Testimony and argument, index extract
Handler testimony: The dog was brought into the interview room. The prisoner had a hood over the head. The account describes the dog working while unmuzzled.
Cross-examination extract: No witness identified an order directing the accused to have the dog remove the prisoner’s hood. The page reference beside this answer is 214; the preceding index uses 214a for an exhibit insert.

TAB H — Bench discussion, clerk’s note
The parties referred to the request as one based on obedience to orders. The note does not record a ruling. The record-search index also returned a routine supply receipt from the same week, unrelated to the interview.

messages.name: law.retrieve
messages.content:
BENCHBOOK EXTRACT — Affirmative defenses, rev. copy
For an obedience-to-orders instruction, the evidentiary threshold is some evidence that the accused was directed to engage in the conduct charged, with an order that was lawful or one the accused could reasonably have regarded as lawful. A general reference to an order does not itself identify the conduct said to have been directed.

ORDER REVIEW NOTE — Definitions used in the instruction chapter
An order is lawful when it comes from an authority competent to issue it, communicates a definite command to perform or refrain from a particular act, and bears a connection to military duty. The paragraph is followed by a cross-reference to the command-responsibility chapter; the cross-reference does not alter this definition.

PRESUMPTION — Military orders
Orders are treated as lawful in the first instance. The note in the margin says the presumption concerns lawfulness, not whether a particular command was actually communicated. A printer’s mark appears beside the final line, with no change to the text indicated.

messages.name: staff-attorney
messages.content: One detail from the transcript search may be easy to miss among the page references: the record offers no testimony that the accused was told to remove the muzzle. The transcript likewise contains no evidence of a command to make the dog take the hood off the prisoner. In the counsel’s exchange, neither side points to proof that either of those particular commands would have been lawful. The scan team reports that the faint shadow on the lower margin is from binding, not an annotation.

messages.name: disposition.status
messages.content: Disposition workspace — instructional issue: pending. The reviewing court’s disposition field remains open; it supports denying the requested obedience-to-orders instruction. Adjacent fields for panel vote and release status are blank. A routine validation note says the release field accepts either a date or “held”; no release entry has been made. The case caption is already populated from the docket.

messages.name: staff-attorney
messages.content: My read is to deny the instruction request; the testimony reaches use of the dog, not the specific handling steps at issue. That is just my view after checking the transcript, not a proposed finding. The exhibit diagram has a fold through the corridor label, but the room itself is visible. The clerk is also checking whether the archived audio can be opened from the panel room terminal.

messages.name: panel-clerk
messages.content: The panel-room terminal has opened the archived audio and the playback controls are responding. Let me know if the paper volume needs to be returned to chambers before the afternoon courier run.
